plugin.perm.secrets: Read passwords and other secret fields
plugin.perm.itemsWrite: Create items and change their fields
plugin.perm.sshSign: Sign with the vault's ssh keys
plugin.state.offHint: The plugin is installed but disabled: no section in the rail, no events, calls are refused.
plugin.locked: “{title}” only works while the vault is unlocked.
plugin.unknown.title: Unknown plugin “{id}”
plugin.unknown.body: The daemon ships a plugin this build of the interface does not know. Update the app.
gen.insideHint: Never start or end with punctuation: other people's forms either trim it or refuse it.
gen.takenHint: The ones that went to the clipboard: almost certainly pasted somewhere.
gen.previousHint: Stored encrypted with the vault key: lock the vault and they are gone from view.
fill.bothHint: The login, then the password, each into its field
autofill.noAccess: To type into other apps keyward needs the Accessibility permission in macOS privacy settings.
spot.tag.site: Items of a site by domain
spot.section.name: Items
spot.tag.name: Items by name
spot.tag.type: Item type: login, card, identity, note, ssh_key
spot.nothingTagged: Nothing for these tags. Backspace puts the tag back into editing.
daemon.down.title: The daemon is not responding
daemon.down.body: Without it ssh falls back to key files as usual.
accounts.title: Accounts
setup.title: Where to connect
login.title: Unlock your vault
unlock.title: Vault is locked
unlock.noTouchId: Touch ID is not set up — enable it in Settings, under Security
twofactor.title: Two-step login
twofactor.unsupported.title: Method not supported
twofactor.unsupported.body: The server asks for {providers}. keyward supports authenticator codes, email codes and YubiKey.
twofactor.prompt.3: Insert the key and press its button
biometric.off: Touch ID is off — you'll type the password every time
biometric.password: Master password to store in Keychain
org.name: Name
org.billingHint: The server insists on this field — it came from cloud Bitwarden. It affects nothing but letters from it.
org.newHint: The organisation gets its own key, encrypted with your public key, and its own RSA pair. The keys are computed here; the server only stores them.
org.deleteWarn: The organisation “{name}” disappears with all its items and collections — for every member and on every device. There is no undo.
org.deleteWhyPassword: The server asks for the master password on such a delete, and it is right to.
collection.deleteWarn: The collection “{name}” disappears for every member. Its items are not deleted, but stop being reachable for anyone whose only access was through it.
member.inviteHint: The invited person accepts the invitation themselves, and then has to be confirmed — only then do they get the organisation key.
member.confirmHint: The organisation key will be encrypted with the member's public key: only they can read it.
member.fingerprintCompare: Ask {name} to read out their fingerprint phrase from their account settings, by phone or in person. Confirm only if every word matches.
member.removeWarn: {name} loses access to every item of the organisation.
trash.noneHint: Deleted items land here. From here they can be restored or finished off.
item.trashConfirm: The item goes to the trash. You can bring it back from there.
item.purgeConfirm: This is final: the item disappears from the server and from every device.
who.title: Title
item.name: Name
item.needName: Give it a name — that is how you will find it
items.emptyHint: Change the query or clear the filter.
edit.sitesHint: The item is found by these in search and filled in the browser.
edit.customHint: Keyward's own fields start with kw-: kw-host binds an ssh key to hosts.
item.favouriteHint: The item rises to the top of the list and lands in Favourites.
edit.repromptHint: Before revealing this item's secrets keyward will ask for the fingerprint.
edit.customEmpty: No custom fields yet. They are for what the ready-made ones have no place for: a recovery code, a contract number, a keyward marker.
edit.kind.text.hint: Visible at once, copied with one press.
edit.kind.hidden.hint: Shown only on demand — like a password.
edit.kind.checkbox.hint: Yes or no. Stored as true or false.
edit.link.title: Title
edit.kind.linked.hint: Mirrors a field of this very item: change the password and this changes too. Autofill needs it when a site names its input its own way.
edit.title: Edit item
edit.name: Name
edit.savedLocally: Saved locally — the server did not answer
edits.emptyHint: Changes that failed to push will show up here.
edits.damagedHint: It cannot be read. Forget it; if it had not been sent, make the change again
edits.lockedHint: Unlock its vault to see what it changes
settings.title: Settings
settings.plugins.catalogHint: What you can install: packages from the registries. A plugin arrives disabled — first it shows what it asks for.
settings.plugins.stale: This list comes from the cache: no registry answered. Installed plugins keep working as before.
settings.plugins.empty.title: Nothing to install yet
settings.plugins.empty.body: Plugins come from registries — addresses with an index.json that lists the packages. None answered and the cache is empty: check the network, or add your own address under “Sources” below.
settings.plugins.installedHint: What sits on disk: built-ins can be switched off, installed ones removed.
settings.plugins.sourcesHint: Registry addresses the catalogue is built from. Only https:// — and file:// for a build of your own.
settings.plugins.sourcesNone: No addresses at all: there is nowhere to take a catalogue from.
settings.plugins.sourceBad: The address has to start with https:// or file://
settings.plugins.sourceDupe: That address is already on the list
settings.plugins.byUrlHint: A link to a .tar.gz. An address outside the registries has no checksum to compare against, and the consent dialog will say so.
settings.plugins.installHint: The developer path: a package directory with plugin.json, or a .zip / .tar.gz archive. It arrives disabled — first it shows what it asks for.
settings.plugins.consent.title: “{name}” asks for
settings.plugins.consent.body: Plugin “{name}” {version} is on disk and disabled. Enabling it means agreeing to what it asks for.
settings.plugins.consent.later: Closing this window is fine too: the plugin stays installed but disabled, and you can enable it whenever you like.
settings.plugins.consent.unverifiedBody: It came from outside the registries: there is no publisher signature and no checksum to compare against. A plugin is an ordinary program and runs with your rights. Enable it only if you trust whoever you got it from.
settings.plugins.consent.addedBody: The update asks for more than the installed version did, which is why it sits disabled: until you agree, it does not run.
settings.plugins.untrustedHint: This publisher's signature is not trusted yet: confirm the key first, then install.
settings.plugins.revoked: This version is revoked: {reason}. It cannot be installed.
settings.plugins.revokedInstalled: This version is revoked: {reason}. The daemon will switch the plugin off on the next catalogue refresh — install a newer version or remove it.
settings.plugins.trust.title: Trust the publisher “{name}”?
settings.plugins.trust.body: The key of “{name}” becomes trusted, and packages it signs — “{plugin}” among them — become installable. This is a decision about all of their plugins, not about one.
settings.plugins.trust.fingerprintHint: Five words, the fingerprint of the key. Compare them with what the publisher shows on their own page: all five matching means the key is the right one.
settings.plugins.removeHint: The package directory goes, and its settings and state go with it.
settings.plugins.remove.title: Remove “{name}”?
settings.plugins.remove.body: The directory of “{name}” will be deleted together with its settings and state. There will be nothing to restore them from — only a fresh install.
settings.lockHint: Keys are forgotten and agent sockets dropped. Counted from the last time the vault was used.
settings.graceHint: How long after a successful Touch ID we stay quiet. Reset when the vault locks.
settings.touchIdSecretsHint: The socket already hands passwords only to the signed keyward window. This is on top: a touch for every reveal and copy, with the same trust window.
settings.touchIdLaunch: Ask for Touch ID on launch
settings.iconsHint: Icons come from the same server as the vault. Turn this off to avoid even those requests.
settings.startOnLoginHint: The daemon always starts on its own — this is about the window.
settings.accentHint: One colour sets the whole theme: grounds, columns, fields, text and highlights. Green, amber and red keep their meaning.
err.pinReset: Five wrong PINs in a row — the PIN was reset. Unlock with the master password and set it again in Settings.
settings.profile.name: Name
settings.fingerprintHint: Five words another person uses to verify they are confirming your key.
settings.passwordHint: Changes together with the encryption key. Every other device will have to log in again.
settings.twofactorHint: A second factor at login: an authenticator app or an email code.
settings.kdfHint: How the encryption key is derived from the master password.
settings.devicesHint: Where the account was logged in from and when it was last active.
settings.exportHint: Unencrypted JSON or CSV in Bitwarden's format — for migration or a backup.
settings.devices.noSingle: Vaultwarden cannot revoke devices one by one — only all at once.
settings.deauthorizeHint: Every session is closed and every device asks for the password again. keyward itself logs back in.
settings.deauthorize.body: The server resets every session and token. keyward logs back in here; other devices will ask for the master password.
settings.purgeHint: Deletes every personal item and folder. Organization items are untouched. Cannot be undone.
settings.purge.body: All personal items and folders are deleted permanently — not to the trash. Organization items stay.
settings.deleteAccountHint: The account and all its data disappear from the server. Cannot be undone.
settings.deleteAccount.body: The account is deleted from the server with every item. keyward forgets it, along with Touch ID and the PIN.
settings.twofactor.afterChange: The server reset the sessions — log in again by confirming the second factor.
settings.password.title: Change master password
settings.password.body: The encryption key is re-encrypted with the new password. Other devices will ask for it at the next login.
settings.password.same: The new password is the same as the current one.
settings.password.hintPlaceholder: Not the password itself — something that reminds you of it
settings.email.title: Change email
settings.email.body: A verification code goes to the new address. The encryption key is re-encrypted: the email is the master key's salt.
settings.email.codeBody: The code was sent to {email}. Enter it to finish the change.
settings.twofactor.title: Two-step login
settings.twofactor.body: Every action is confirmed with the master password — the server requires it on each request.
settings.twofactor.recoveryHint: A single code for when the second factor is unavailable. Write it down separately.
settings.twofactor.authBody: The server issues a secret for an authenticator app (Aegis, Raivo, 1Password, Google Authenticator).
settings.twofactor.scan: Scan the code with the app or type the secret by hand, then enter the six-digit code.
settings.twofactor.qrAlt: QR code for the authenticator app
settings.twofactor.emailBody: A code will be emailed at every login.
settings.twofactor.recoveryBody: The recovery code removes the second factor entirely — keep it like a password.
settings.twofactor.recoveryShown: Copy it and put it somewhere safe. Using it turns the second factor off.
settings.twofactor.disableBody: “{name}” will be turned off. If it is the only method, login falls back to the password alone.
settings.kdf.title: Key derivation function
settings.kdf.body: Argon2id resists GPU brute force better; PBKDF2 is what Bitwarden has always used.
settings.kdf.iterationsHint: The server accepts 100,000 to 2,000,000; OWASP recommends at least 600,000.
settings.kdf.warn: Changing the KDF logs every device out; on a weak phone, high Argon2id parameters can make login very slow.
settings.devices.body: Devices that logged in. A single one cannot be removed — only all at once, in the danger zone.
settings.export.title: Export vault
settings.export.body: Personal and organization items from the decrypted snapshot. The file gets 0600 permissions.
settings.export.jsonHint: Bitwarden JSON: imports back losslessly, including custom fields and folders.
settings.export.csvHint: Bitwarden CSV: logins and notes; cards and identities keep only name and notes.
settings.export.warn: The file is not encrypted: every password is in plain text. Delete it when you are done.
settings.pin.on: Unlocks with a PIN. Five wrong tries in a row reset it.
settings.pin.off: A short code instead of the master password on this computer.
settings.lockAction.lockHint: Keys are forgotten, the login token stays — only the master password is needed.
settings.lockAction.logoutHint: The account logs out entirely: tokens reset, a full login on return. Touch ID and PIN stay.
settings.pin.title: Turn on PIN
settings.pin.body: The master password is encrypted with a key derived from the PIN and stored on this computer. Five wrong tries in a row reset the PIN.
settings.hideOnCopyHint: Copy something and the window gets out of the way, like Bitwarden.
settings.keepInTrayHint: The close button hides the window into the menu bar. When this and “Keep in the Dock” are both off, the close button quits the app, agent included.
settings.keepInDock: Keep in the Dock when closed
settings.keepInDockHint: On — the icon stays in the Dock after the close button. Off — it leaves the Dock with the window and comes back when the window opens
settings.screenCaptureHint: By default the window is black in screenshots, screen recordings and Zoom sharing.
settings.newInterfaceHint: The window reloads into the new interface. To come back, use the account menu. KEYWARD_UI=new|old at launch overrides this setting
settings.security.clipboardHint: Passwords and codes are cleared after 30 seconds unless replaced. Usernames and card expiry stay: they get pasted more than once.
settings.security.lockHint: Keys are forgotten and agent sockets are dropped. The login token stays — only the master password is needed.
hashicorp.notesOnly: Only secure notes are listed: logins and cards have nowhere to keep an address and keys.
hashicorp.probeFirst: Enter the address and press Check — the server will say how many keys it needs
hashicorp.title: HashiCorp Vault
err.badTwoFactor: That two-step code did not work
passkey.title: Passkeys ({n})
passkey.removeConfirm: Signing in with this key stops working immediately and cannot be recovered: the private key exists only here. Register a new one on the site before deleting.
passkey.hint: The private key stays encrypted inside the item and never leaves keyward. Sites use it through the keyward browser extension, with Touch ID every time.
detail.empty: Pick an item on the left
detail.historyClearConfirm: The earlier passwords of this login are removed for good. The current password stays.
detail.historyClearHint: The login's earlier passwords are deleted from the vault on every device. If a site still uses one of them, you will no longer find it here.
detail.historyHint: The passwords this login had before, newest first. Bitwarden keeps the last five.
vault.unsealKeysHint: Shamir needs a threshold — three keys out of five, for example. The rest are optional.
secret.pasteEnvHint: KEY=VALUE lines; “export” and quotes are stripped. Recognised: {n}.
policy.editHint: HCL as in Vault: path and capabilities. Saving replaces the body; tokens with this policy get the new rights immediately.
policy.bodyHint: Built from the choices above. Edit it by hand and the choices stop overwriting it.
vault.policiesHint: Comma separated. With no policy the token inherits the broker's rights — not allowed.
err.undecryptable: Could not decrypt the field — sync the vault
err.totpLinkUnreadable: Could not read the otpauth link: {reason}
err.totpCodeFailed: Could not generate the one-time code: {reason}
err.totpLooksLikeCode: This looks like a one-time code, not the secret it is made of. Paste the secret key or the otpauth:// link
err.totpNothingToRestore: The edit history has no earlier TOTP secret for this item — paste the secret again from the site
err.totpSeedBadAlphabet: Could not read the one-time-code key: {outside} of its {total} characters are not base32. It looks like the field holds a caption or part of a link rather than the key itself — leave only the key, or paste the whole otpauth:// link
err.totpSeedTruncated: Could not read the one-time-code key: {total} base32 characters do not make a whole block. It looks like the key was copied only in part
err.peerNotKeyward: Only keyward's own programs are let in, and this process is not one of them
err.peerBridgePasskeysOnly: The browser bridge may only use passkeys
err.pluginForeignField: The password goes out only when the keyward app asks for it; an external plugin reads its own kw-* fields and nothing else
err.pluginReprompt: This item is marked «ask for the password again», so an external plugin does not get it
touch.passwordToApp: Give the password to the keyward app
err.touchIdUnavailable: Touch ID is unavailable ({reason}) — type the master password
err.touchIdTimeout: Touch ID waited and got no answer
err.kdfArgon2Memory: Argon2id takes between 16 and 1024 MiB of memory
err.kdfArgon2Parallelism: Argon2id takes a parallelism between 1 and 16
err.kdfOutOfRange: The account's key derivation settings are outside safe limits, so the password was not used. The server may be misconfigured or not genuine
err.reloginFailed: The change went through, but logging in again did not: {reason}
err.noAccountId: The snapshot has no account identifier — sync the vault
err.publicKeyEncode: The public key will not encode: {reason}
err.nameTooLong: A name longer than 50 characters is one the server will not take
err.colorFormat: A colour has to look like #rrggbb
err.passwordTooShort: The new master password is shorter than 12 characters
err.passwordUnchanged: The new master password is the same as the current one
err.rbwDbNotSaved: The rbw database will not save: {reason}
err.emailUnchanged: That is the current email address
err.emailCodeRequired: The code from the letter is needed
err.kdfUnchanged: Those KDF parameters are already in force
err.authCodeRequired: The code from the app is needed
err.noRecoveryCode: There is no recovery code yet; it appears once the second factor is on
err.noOrgKey: There is no key for that organisation
err.noOrgKeySync: There is no key for that organisation — sync the vault
err.itemKeyLocked: The item key would not open; not writing, so as not to spoil it
err.itemNotFoundSync: The item was not found — sync the vault
err.rbwDbNotRead: The rbw database will not read: {reason}
err.rbwConfigNotSaved: The rbw config will not save: {reason}
err.noPendingLogin: There is no login in progress — start again
err.codeNotSent: The server did not send the code: {reason}
err.nothingToUnlock: There is nothing to unlock: log in and sync first
err.syncFailed: The sync did not go through: {reason}
err.itemNeedsName: An item has to have a name
err.itemKindNotCreatable: An item of that kind cannot be created
err.noKeysForItem: There are no keys for that item
err.passkeyGone: That passkey is no longer in the item — sync the vault
err.pluginProtocolOld: The plugin {plugin} speaks an old, unencrypted protocol: update it
err.daemonNotOurs: The process on the control socket is not keyward's daemon
err.daemonKeyMissing: The daemon's key was not found: is keyward running?
err.channelRequired: This client speaks the old, unencrypted protocol: update keyward
err.channelTooLong: The message is too long for the channel
err.channelFailed: The encrypted channel to the daemon broke off
err.passwordHistoryEmpty: The login has no old passwords to forget
err.sshDraftGone: The generated key is gone: generate it again
err.pluginUnknownOp: The plugin does not know the action {op}
err.orgForbidden: The organisation cannot be managed from this account
err.accentColorBad: The accent colour must be written as #rrggbb
err.editDamaged: The edit is damaged and cannot be opened
err.passkeyUsesDamaged: The journal of passkey sign-ins cannot be read and was left untouched
err.editOtherAccount: This edit belongs to another account: switch to it first
err.daemonNotRunning: keyward is not running: open the keyward app
err.passkeyHost: keyward did not understand the answer to a passkey request
err.passkeyBadRequest: The site's passkey request is malformed
err.passkeyInsecureOrigin: Passkeys work only on secure (https) pages
err.passkeyBadOrigin: The page's address cannot be used for a passkey
err.passkeyBusy: Another passkey request is already waiting for Touch ID
err.passkeyNeedsLogin: A passkey can only be saved into a login
err.passkeyExists: The vault already has a passkey for this account on the site
err.passkeyAlgorithm: The site accepts no key keyward can make: only ES256 is supported
err.passkeyUnsupportedKey: This passkey's key is of a kind keyward cannot use
err.passkeyDamaged: The passkey is damaged and cannot be used
err.passkeyWrongSite: This passkey belongs to another site
err.itemCreatedButMissing: The item was created but could not be found — sync the vault
err.orgNeedsName: An organisation has to have a name
err.billingEmailRequired: A billing email is needed: the server asks for one
err.orgKeyNotGenerated: The organisation key would not generate: {reason}
err.privateKeyEncode: The private key will not encode: {reason}
err.memberKeyNotBase64: The member's public key is not base64: {reason}
err.memberKeyUnparsable: The member's public key will not parse: {reason}
err.fingerprintChanged: The member's key changed after its fingerprint was shown, so nothing was sealed. Open the confirm again and compare the new words with them
err.noPrivateKey: The snapshot has no private key — sync the vault
err.privateKeyLocked: The private key did not decrypt
err.deleteOnlyFromTrash: Only what is already in the trash can be deleted for good
err.notAPluginPackage: {url} does not look like a plugin package: a .tar.gz or a .zip is expected
err.sourceScheme: The address «{url}» is neither https:// nor file://
err.pluginVersionRevoked: Version {version} of the plugin «{plugin}» was revoked: {reason}. One like that cannot be installed
err.packageDigestMismatch: The package fingerprint did not match the showcase: it promised {promised}, {got} was downloaded. The installation was called off
err.packageSignatureMismatch: The package «{plugin}» is not signed with the key of the publisher «{publisher}»; the installation was called off
err.packageUnsigned: The package «{plugin}» is in the showcase unsigned; only signed packages are installed from a showcase
err.publisherChanged: The installed version was signed by the publisher «{installed}» and the update by «{update}». That does not happen: remove the plugin if you really want somebody else's build
err.publisherUnknown: The publisher «{publisher}» is unknown. Check the five words of their fingerprint with the author and trust them («Trust publisher»), or write the key into {file} by hand; otherwise this package cannot be installed
err.pluginIdTooLong: The identifier is longer than {max} characters: «{id}»
err.pluginIdCharset: The identifier «{id}» has something in it besides lower-case latin letters, digits and a hyphen
err.pluginIdHyphen: The identifier «{id}» starts or ends with a hyphen
err.pluginIdReserved: The identifier «{id}» is taken by a file of keyward's own
err.pluginNoExec: The manifest does not say what to run the plugin with (the exec field)
err.pluginExecAbsolute: The exec «{exec}» is an absolute path; the program has to lie inside the package
err.pluginExecOutside: The exec «{exec}» leads outside the package
err.pluginExecNotAFile: The exec «{exec}» is not a file
err.pluginVersionFormat: The version «{version}» is not three numbers with dots (1.0.0, for instance)
err.pluginIconCharset: The icon «{icon}» will not do: lower-case latin letters, digits and a hyphen, up to 32 characters
err.pluginTitleTooLong: The title is longer than 64 characters
err.pluginDescriptionTooLong: The description is longer than 200 characters
err.packageVersionMismatch: The showcase promised version {promised} and the package holds {found}; the installation was called off
err.packageExtraPermissions: The package asks for more than the showcase listed: {permissions}; the installation was called off
err.pluginAlreadyInstalled: The plugin «{id}» is already installed; remove it before installing it again
err.pluginIdBuiltin: «{id}» is built into keyward; a plugin cannot be installed under that name
err.archiveNoManifest: The archive has no {manifest}; this is not a plugin package
err.archiveManyPackages: The archive holds {count} packages at once; one is needed
err.pluginInstalledNotRegistered: The plugin «{id}» was installed but did not reach the register
err.publisherKeyUndeclared: The showcase declared no key for the publisher «{publisher}», so there is nothing to trust. Refresh the showcase or write the key into {file} by hand
err.pluginBuiltinOnlyOff: «{id}» is built into keyward; it can only be switched off
err.itemNoPrivateKey: The item «{name}» has no private key; there is nothing to sign with
touch.sshSign: Sign a login with the key «{name}»
touch.passkeyRegister: Save a passkey for {user} on {site} in {browser}
touch.passkeySignInPlain: Sign in to {site} with a passkey in {browser}
notice.pluginDisabled.title: The plugin «{plugin}» was switched off
notice.publisherUntrusted.body: The publisher «{publisher}» is no longer trusted; there is nothing to check updates with
err.pluginSilent: The plugin «{plugin}» has been silent for over {seconds}s
err.pluginGone: The plugin «{plugin}» fell away without answering
notice.pluginOff.title: A plugin was switched off
notice.pluginCrashed.body: «{plugin}» ended with an error three times in a minute
err.setupNeedsUrlAndLogin: The server address and the login are needed
err.serverUrlScheme: A server address has to start with http:// or https://
err.keychainPasswordStale: The password from the keychain did not fit ({reason}); the master password has probably changed
err.pinPasswordStale: The password under the PIN did not fit ({reason}); set the PIN again
err.graceOverAnHour: The fingerprint's window of trust cannot be longer than an hour
err.lockTimeoutZero: The automatic lock's interval cannot be zero
err.lockTimeoutOverADay: Longer than a day is «never»; choose that explicitly
err.clipboardClearOverAnHour: Clearing the clipboard more than an hour later means nothing
field.name: Name
err.generatorNoSet: At least one set of characters is needed
err.generatorTooShort: A password shorter than four characters means nothing
err.generatorTooLong: More than a hundred and twenty-eight characters is of use to nobody
err.generatorEdgesImpossible: There is nothing to cover the edges with: nothing but punctuation is chosen
err.generatorInsideNeedsThree: Keeping punctuation inside takes at least three characters
err.generatorNothingLeft: Leaving the look-alike characters out left nothing
err.generatorFewerThanSets: There are fewer characters than the sets chosen
err.generatorCannotKeepInside: At this length the punctuation cannot be kept inside — take a longer one, or add letters and digits
err.chosenFieldEmpty: The chosen field is empty; there is nothing to type
err.noTargetField: There is no target field: press Cmd+Shift+L inside a field of the program you want
err.noLoginForm: No login form here: a login field next to a password field is needed to type both. Type them one at a time
err.noPluginCard: The daemon returned no plugin card
err.daemonCannotTrustYet: The daemon cannot add publishers yet: update keyward
folder.name: Name
folder.nameHint: Visible only to you: the name is encrypted with your key.
folder.deleteWarn: The folder “{name}” will be deleted on every device. Its {n} items are not deleted — they stay in the vault without a folder.
org.readOnlyHint: Your role here is “{role}”: only the owner changes the name and the billing.
org.deleteZoneHint: The organisation, its items and collections disappear for every member. Your master password is asked for.
item.needKindPart: The key is not ready yet — generate one or paste a valid private key
err.sshKeyRequired: An SSH key item needs a key: generate one or paste your own
err.sshKeyNotAKeyItem: This item is not an SSH key, so it has no key to replace
err.sshKeyGenerate: The key could not be made: {reason}
err.sshKeyIsPublic: That is the public half of a key (ssh-…). Paste the private one — the file without .pub
err.sshKeyUnreadable: The private key is damaged or cut short: paste the whole file, from BEGIN to END
err.sshKeyNeedsPassphrase: The key is under a passphrase: enter it below
err.sshKeyWrongPassphrase: The passphrase does not open this key
err.sshKeyPemEncrypted: An encrypted PEM key cannot be read. Convert it first: ssh-keygen -p -f <file> (it rewrites the file in OpenSSH format)
err.sshKeyUnsupported: This is not a private key keyward can read: OpenSSH, or RSA in PEM (PKCS#1 or PKCS#8)
folder.deleteHint: The folder goes away; its items ({n}) stay, without a folder.
err.orgNotFound: The organisation is not in the vault: sync and try again
err.orgRoleNotYours: Your role in the organisation does not let you give this role
err.memberAccessAllWithCollections: Access to every collection and a list of collections at once: choose one
err.memberCollectionTwice: The same collection is given twice
err.passphraseTooShort: A passphrase needs at least three words
err.passphraseTooLong: A passphrase of more than twenty words fits no form
err.passphraseBadSeparator: The separator is one character, or none
err.passphraseWordList: The word list for passphrases is damaged
err.collectionsNeedOrg: Only an organisation's item lies in collections
err.collectionRequired: An organisation's item needs at least one collection
err.collectionNotFound: That collection is not in the vault; sync and try again
err.collectionNotInOrg: That collection belongs to another organisation
